stories.h: EFCC Probes N100bn Benue Technical College Contracts
stories.e: The EFCC is investigating alleged fraud in over N100 billion worth of technical college contracts in Benue State after more than 60 contractors filed petitions claiming they were defrauded. Four senior state officials, including the current and a former education commissioner, have been questioned, and investigators are examining claims that contracts bypassed the governor's approval and that a 1% vetting fee was improperly demanded.

stories.h: Police Service Commission dismisses three senior officers, demotes 16 others over misconduct
stories.e: Nigeria's Police Service Commission dismissed three senior police officers and demoted 16 others at a plenary session in Abuja, while handing out reprimands to 23 more officers and clearing three of wrongdoing. Commission chairman Hashimu Argungu said the decisions reflect a zero-tolerance stance on corruption, human rights abuses and improper interference in civil disputes by officers, though the commission did not publicly name those punished.

stories.h: Sowore Rejects Police Arrests Over Ekiti Attack on Him, Alleges Cover-Up
stories.e: Activist Omoyele Sowore has dismissed the police's arrest of 11 suspects in connection with an attack on him in Ekiti State, accusing authorities of shielding the real perpetrators. He says the arrests appear designed to create an impression of accountability without genuinely investigating who ordered or carried out the attack.

stories.h: Customs Seizes N6.19bn in Smuggled Goods, Warns Machetes Pose Election Security Risk
stories.e: The Nigeria Customs Service's Lagos-based Federal Operations Unit says it blocked 195 smuggling attempts worth about N6.19 billion between late September and early November, recovering over N683 million in additional duties. Among the seized items were thousands of machetes that the unit's acting comptroller warned could pose security risks ahead of upcoming elections.

stories.h: Federal Government's Q1 2026 Revenue Falls 45% Short Despite Oil Price Gains
stories.e: Nigeria's federal government collected just N5.08 trillion in the first quarter of 2026, a drop of nearly 45 percent, even though global oil prices were higher during the period. The shortfall raises fresh questions about revenue leakage and fiscal management at a time when debt servicing continues to consume a large share of government spending.

stories.h: Federal Government misses nearly half of Q1 2026 revenue target despite oil price gains
stories.e: Nigeria's federal government collected N5.08 trillion in the first quarter of 2026, falling roughly 45 percent short of target even though higher oil prices were expected to boost receipts. The shortfall raises fresh questions about the reliability of the government's revenue projections and budget assumptions. It comes as officials continue to defend heavy new borrowing plans to cover spending gaps.

stories.h: EFCC uncovers Chinese-run illegal oil refinery in Ogun State
stories.e: Anti-graft operatives from the EFCC's Lagos office raided an abandoned facility in Ogere, Ogun State, believed to have been used by Chinese nationals to illegally refine sludge oil sourced from Warri and Port Harcourt into diesel for sale in Nigeria. Investigators found processing tanks and waste at the site, but no one was present when it was discovered on October 31. The find follows an earlier EFCC raid in the same area that netted 14 Chinese nationals over illegal lithium processing.

stories.h: BudgIT: States left N26.6trn unspent in H1 2026 despite record FAAC inflows
stories.e: A new BudgIT analysis found that 34 states spent only about 24% of their approved 2026 budgets in the first half of the year, even as their federal allocations more than tripled since 2022. BudgIT's country director called for closer scrutiny of why rising state revenue has not translated into better infrastructure, health or education outcomes for residents.

stories.h: World Bank: Nigerian states spend more on roads than on education and healthcare
stories.e: At the launch of BudgIT's 11th State of States report, a World Bank representative said Nigerian state governments have consistently prioritised road and transport spending over education, health and social protection, even as their revenues rose sharply after 2023's subsidy removal and currency reforms. The report found only two states can cover recurrent spending from their own revenue, with the rest reliant on federal transfers.

stories.h: Edo spent N14.5bn on security in 9 months while starving its security ministry of funding
stories.e: Edo State's own third-quarter budget report shows it spent N14.48 billion on security votes and services between January and September 2026, yet released zero naira in capital funding to the Ministry of Public Security and Safety. Equipment such as body cameras and a planned security database for the state's security corps went unfunded as a result.

stories.h: UK appeals court upholds £101.5m confiscation order against ex-Delta governor Ibori
stories.e: The UK Court of Appeal has rejected former Delta State governor James Ibori's bid to reduce a £101.51 million asset confiscation order, ruling that an inflation adjustment applied to his frozen accounts was not disproportionate. Ibori, convicted in 2012 of fraud and money laundering while in office, had sought to cut the order by about £4.3 million.

stories.h: NCDC says N10 billion emergency fund covers more than Ebola response
stories.e: NCDC Director-General Jide Idris pushed back on criticism that a N10 billion emergency fund approved by the federal government has gone unused, explaining the money is meant to cover wider public health threats such as Lassa fever, not Ebola preparedness alone. The clarification followed demands by opposition figures, including Atiku Abubakar, for a full public accounting of how the fund has been spent. Idris said some isolation and treatment centres nationwide still need repairs before they can be considered ready for use.

stories.h: EFCC arraigns man and firm over alleged N12.5 billion fraud in Lagos
stories.e: The EFCC arraigned Adonu Kingsley Ifeanyi and his firm, S Mobile Netzone Limited, before a Lagos Federal High Court on five counts of obtaining money by false pretences, alleging the company funnelled over N12.5 billion in suspected illegal investment scheme proceeds through its accounts between 2020 and 2022. The firm was among 58 companies the EFCC had publicly flagged in 2025 over suspected Ponzi-style operations. Both defendants pleaded not guilty and were granted bail pending trial.

stories.h: NHRC warns unpunished electoral offenders threaten free and fair 2027 polls
stories.e: The National Human Rights Commission Executive Secretary, Tony Ojukwu, told a visiting UN delegation that the failure to prosecute electoral offenders is undermining accountability ahead of the 2027 elections, noting many offenders act on behalf of powerful politicians who escape scrutiny. He criticised the government for ignoring a long-standing Uwais committee recommendation to set up a dedicated electoral offences framework. The NHRC said it is drafting new conduct advisories for politicians, security agencies and civic actors as campaign tensions rise.

stories.h: Cashier testifies in ex-Taraba governor's N27bn diversion trial
stories.e: At the EFCC trial of former Taraba governor Darius Ishaku, a state government cashier testified that he moved local government funds through his own company's bank account on instructions from superiors, describing the transfers as 'official payments.' The case concerns an alleged N27 billion diversion from state coffers during Ishaku's tenure, which he and a co-defendant deny. The trial was adjourned to November 5.

stories.h: INEC uncovers fraudulent voter registrations by its own officials
stories.e: INEC's ICT director said the commission's biometric system flagged roughly 1.5 million of over 11 million new 2026 voter registrations as suspicious, including profiles with AI-generated photos. About 1.28 million of those have already been confirmed fake and purged from the register. INEC has cut system access for implicated registration officials while it reviews evidence for possible disciplinary action.

stories.h: INEC says it is cleaning voter register after AI-generated photo irregularities surface
stories.e: Nigeria's electoral commission acknowledged that suspicious, AI-generated-looking images turned up on some entries in its preliminary voter register ahead of the 2027 elections, which it blames on registration officers rather than any INEC use of AI. The commission says the irregular photos are being stripped out before the register is finalised on December 15, though opposition figures are demanding an independent forensic audit.

stories.h: Nigeria's 2026 debt servicing bill outstrips five key sector budgets combined
stories.e: An analysis of the 2026 federal budget found that Nigeria set aside about N15.8 trillion for debt servicing, roughly N3.16 trillion more than the combined allocations for agriculture, health, works, defence and education. Debt servicing now accounts for about 23% of the entire N68.32tn budget, making it the single largest spending line and raising fresh questions about the government's spending priorities.

stories.h: Nasarawa police detain three men impersonating ICPC officials
stories.e: Police in Nasarawa State detained three men during a routine patrol stop near Lafia after one presented a forged identity card claiming membership of the Independent Corrupt Practices Commission. Investigators say the suspects could not account for the unregistered vehicle they were travelling in, and one has been linked to a banned secret society; all three remain in custody pending prosecution.

stories.h: SERAP urges Tinubu to order probe into suspected AI-generated voter photos
stories.e: Civil society group SERAP has asked President Tinubu to order an independent investigation into suspected AI-generated images that surfaced on multiple voter profiles in INEC's preliminary register ahead of the 2027 elections. The call adds to pressure from opposition figures and civic groups seeking a forensic audit, after INEC acknowledged irregular images but attributed them to registration officers misusing database access rather than confirming AI involvement.

stories.h: Senate gives state assemblies until 15 November to send in resolutions on state police
stories.e: The Senate has set 15 November as the deadline for state Houses of Assembly to formally transmit their resolutions on the proposed constitutional amendment creating state police forces. Senate Leader Opeyemi Bamidele said roughly 30 of Nigeria's 36 state assemblies have already approved and sent in their resolutions, leaving a handful, including Kano, Oyo and Benue, still outstanding.

stories.h: Reps advance bill capping advance rent landlords can demand in Abuja
stories.e: The House of Representatives passed a second reading of a bill that would bar landlords, agents and property managers in the FCT from demanding more than 12 months' rent upfront from tenants, unless the tenant voluntarily agrees in writing to pay more. Sponsored by lawmakers from Enugu and Katsina, the bill next heads to committee for further scrutiny and a public hearing before any final vote.

stories.h: Bayelsa Governor Presents N1.24 Trillion Budget for 2027, Prioritises Capital Spending
stories.e: Governor Douye Diri has presented a N1.24 trillion budget proposal for 2027 to the Bayelsa State House of Assembly, with 68 percent earmarked for capital projects rather than recurrent costs. The proposal marks another significant jump from the state's N1.01 trillion 2026 budget, continuing a pattern of rapid spending growth in recent years.

stories.h: Senate Gives Six Reluctant States Until November 15 to Ratify State Police Bill
stories.e: The Senate has set a November 15 deadline for six state Houses of Assembly that have yet to ratify the constitutional amendment creating state police forces. The bill needs approval from at least 24 of the 36 state assemblies before it can proceed toward becoming law, and lawmakers are pressing holdout states to act quickly.

stories.h: Tinubu Drops $20.5bn Borrowing Plan, Seeks Senate Approval for Fresh $7.7bn Loan Instead
stories.e: President Bola Tinubu has withdrawn his earlier request for National Assembly approval to borrow about $20.5 billion and 1.05 billion euros, replacing it with a new request for roughly $7.7 billion, mainly through Eurobonds. The funds are meant to help cover the external borrowing component of the 2026 budget deficit, covering infrastructure, defence, agriculture, healthcare, power and education projects.

stories.h: Senate rejects reviving Nigeria Air deal, pushes for direct flights to China instead
stories.e: Nigeria's Senate declined to revisit contracts tied to the defunct Nigeria Air national carrier project awarded under the Buhari administration, calling further debate on the matter unproductive. Lawmakers still want a national carrier eventually, but their immediate focus shifted to a motion directing the aviation ministry to renegotiate Nigeria's air services agreement with China so local airlines can fly direct routes there. Relevant committees have four weeks to report back on progress.

stories.h: PDP alleges harassment, detention of its members by Ebonyi governor's administration
stories.e: A PDP state chairpersons' leader told Channels Television that party members in Ebonyi have faced threats, arrests, and property seizures, including the continued detention since mid-October of the party's state women's leader. He also alleged a governorship candidate was barred from campaigning after threats, and that a youth leader's hotel was sealed after he declined to defect to the ruling party. The claims, which remain unverified by independent sources, add to a string of opposition complaints about pressure from state governments ahead of planned elections.

stories.h: ADC accuses Sokoto governor of intimidation ahead of Atiku campaign launch
stories.e: The African Democratic Congress says Governor Ahmed Aliyu's administration is targeting its members in Sokoto, pointing to an alleged attack on a governorship candidate's convoy and the sealing of a campaign office the party planned to use. The party says it will hold the governor responsible for any further violence, while the state government and the ruling party dispute that the incidents were politically motivated. Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar separately accused state security of recruiting protesters to disrupt the event, an allegation officials have not addressed.

stories.h: National Assembly weighs bill for 74 extra seats reserved for women
stories.e: A Constitution Review Committee proposal under consideration would add 37 special Senate seats and 37 House seats for women nationwide, plus three extra reserved seats in each State House of Assembly, running for 16 years before review. Senate Leader Opeyemi Bamidele says the bill is still being worked on and will require concurrence from state assemblies before it can take effect.

stories.h: Senate rejects reviving Nigeria Air, pushes for direct flights to China instead
stories.e: Nigeria's Senate voted down a proposal to resurrect the stalled Nigeria Air project tied to a contract scandal from the Buhari era, calling further debate on it unproductive. Lawmakers instead asked the Tinubu administration to renegotiate its air services agreement with China so Nigerian carriers can fly there directly, while still urging the aviation ministry to explore a new national carrier.

stories.h: Sokoto government seals ADC campaign office amid rising political tension
stories.e: The Sokoto State government sealed an opposition ADC campaign office on Monday, with officials citing a disputed ownership claim tied to a defunct bank and the need to 'protect lives and property' after a clash involving ADC supporters. The move comes amid escalating friction between the state government and the ADC, whose presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar has separately alleged a plot against his party's activities in the state.

stories.h: PDP expels two Gombe governorship aspirants over challenge to Pantami candidacy
stories.e: The PDP expelled Gombe governorship aspirants Khamisu Mailantarki and Usman Garry after a disciplinary panel found they engaged in anti-party conduct while continuing to contest the process that produced former minister Isa Pantami as the party nominee for the 2027 Gombe race. Both men had already lost a court-ordered rerun primary to Pantami in September. Garry is still pursuing a separate suit against INEC over the candidate list.

stories.h: Senate Leader Bamidele: NASS weighing proposal for 74 extra seats for women
stories.e: Senate Leader Opeyemi Bamidele says the National Assembly constitution review committee is considering a proposal to create 74 additional legislative seats reserved for women across the Senate and House of Representatives, plus more seats in state assemblies. Similar reserved-seats proposals have stalled at committee stage in earlier sessions. Advocates argue the move could help close Nigeria wide gender gap in elected office.

stories.h: Plateau governor inaugurates APC's 2027 campaign council
stories.e: Governor Caleb Mutfwang formally launched the APC's campaign council for the 2027 general election in Plateau State, signalling the ruling party's early mobilisation in the North-Central region. The move adds to a wave of campaign structures being set up by state governors well ahead of the 2027 polls.

stories.h: Atiku, Kwankwaso trade jabs over who should step aside ahead of 2027
stories.e: In an escalating fight over opposition strategy for the 2027 election, Atiku Abubakar is pressing President Tinubu to relinquish power, while Kwankwaso is instead urging Atiku himself to step aside for a different opposition candidate. The dispute underscores ongoing fractures within Nigeria's opposition camp heading into the next election cycle.

stories.h: Umahi says South-East has no credible 2027 presidential candidate, backs Tinubu
stories.e: Ebonyi Governor Dave Umahi declared that the South-East currently has no presidential candidate capable of winning the 2027 race, arguing the region's turn has not yet arrived and urging Igbo voters to back President Tinubu's re-election bid instead. The remarks extend an ongoing dispute between Umahi and other South-East political figures, including Labour Party's Peter Obi, over the region's electoral strategy.

stories.h: APC campaign defends Tinubu's 2023 electricity pledge ahead of 2027 scorecard
stories.e: Facing renewed criticism over an unmet 2023 promise to end estimated billing and guarantee stable power, the APC Presidential Campaign Council says Tinubu's pledge was always conditional and points to the 2023 Electricity Act, a N4 trillion bond plan to clear inherited power-sector debts, and metering progress as evidence of movement. The party acknowledges Nigeria's chronic power problems remain unresolved as Tinubu prepares to seek re-election in 2027.

stories.h: Opposition parties allege intimidation, blocked venues as 2027 campaign heats up
stories.e: Opposition figures in several states say they are facing a pattern of billboard destruction, denied access to public venues and even violence as 2027 campaigning intensifies, including a death during a rally in Enugu and claims that a Sokoto hotel was paid to deny an opposition party lodging. A lawyer and former presidential aide pushed back, urging parties to submit concrete evidence rather than generalise from isolated incidents.

stories.h: Enugu clerics disown APC campaign list, demand removal of their names
stories.e: The Catholic Diocese of Enugu and the Enugu chapter of the Christian Association of Nigeria say the ruling APC added a bishop and other clergy to a faith-based campaign group for the state governorship race without their consent. Church officials called the move unauthorised and warned of legal action unless their names are withdrawn, saying the listing falsely implies a partisan endorsement by institutions that are meant to stay neutral in politics.

stories.h: Atiku presses INEC on voter register as Tinubu defends fresh $20.5bn borrowing plan
stories.e: In a roundup of Friday political developments, Atiku Abubakar and the NDC pushed the electoral commission to correct irregularities in the roughly 103-million-strong voters register before next year election, while INEC pledged fixes ahead of certification. Separately, President Tinubu defended his request to the National Assembly for about $20.5 billion and over one billion euros in fresh external loans, arguing the funds are needed for development projects. Both developments reflect mounting pre-election tension over electoral transparency and the administration debt strategy.

stories.h: Delta leads states in latest FAAC allocations as Lagos slips to fifth
stories.e: Nigeria's 36 states shared a combined ₦1.07 trillion in net FAAC allocations for August revenue, with Delta topping the table at ₦98.27 billion on the strength of oil derivation payments. Lagos, long the top earner from VAT, fell to fifth place as its growth lagged other states and deductions for debt and VAT adjustments cut into its take. The top ten states, mostly oil producers, cornered nearly half of all disbursements, underscoring how derivation revenue continues to concentrate public funds among a few states.

stories.h: Cooking gas to cost more as Dangote Refinery raises LPG gantry price to N1,000/kg
stories.e: Dangote Refinery lifted its LPG gantry price by 8.1% to N1,000 per kilogram, even as Lagos depots were already selling at N1,450/kg. Industry players warn the increase could stall Nigeria's shift away from firewood and kerosene toward cleaner cooking gas, despite a 17.78% year-on-year rise in domestic LPG supply.

stories.h: Nigeria's private sector activity expands for a fifth straight month as PMI hits 53.2
stories.e: The CBN's October purchasing managers survey shows Nigeria's composite PMI climbing to 53.2 from 53.0 in September, marking a fifth consecutive month of growth in business activity. Agriculture led the expansion for a 27th straight month and industry grew for a third month running, while services activity, though still expanding, slowed slightly compared with the previous month.

stories.h: NNPC Plans to Sell Up to 10% Stake in Landmark IPO, Eyes Transparency Over Cash
stories.e: Nigeria's state oil firm NNPC is preparing to sell between 5 and 10 percent of itself to mostly domestic investors in an initial public offering, with preparations likely stretching through 2027. Company officials say the main goal is improving transparency and governance rather than raising money, following a model similar to Abu Dhabi's national oil company.

stories.h: Explainer: What Tinubu's new $21.7bn loan request means for Nigerians
stories.e: President Tinubu's administration is seeking a fresh $21.7 billion in external borrowing at a time when Nigeria's total public debt already stands near N166.8 trillion. The request renews debate over whether new loans will fund visible improvements in roads, power, and public services, or simply add to a debt-service burden taxpayers already carry. Lawmakers and analysts are expected to scrutinize the terms and intended projects before any approval proceeds.

stories.h: Fewer than 10 percent of Nigerian properties have proper land titles, says finance official
stories.e: Armstrong Takang, managing director of Ministry of Finance Incorporated, told a House of Representatives housing conference that fewer than 10 percent of properties nationwide have proper land titles, which he said weakens credit access and investor confidence. He linked the gap to a lending-to-GDP ratio of 12.9 percent, far below the sub-Saharan African average, and cited more than 270 recorded building-collapse deaths tied to weak regulatory oversight. Lawmakers at the event discussed a bill to create a National Real Estate Regulatory Authority to centralise property records.

stories.h: Nigeria launches USSD credit service for Nigerians without smartphones
stories.e: The Nigerian Consumer Credit Corporation, CREDICORP, launched SPARK, a USSD credit service dialled via star347star333hash, letting Nigerians without smartphones or internet access borrow for essentials such as solar equipment, mobility and household goods. Chief executive Uzoma Nwagba said the scheme targets first-time borrowers with little credit history so they can build repayment records. CREDICORP says it has disbursed over N61 billion to more than 353,000 Nigerians through its programmes as of October 31, though these figures are self-reported by the agency.

stories.h: Reps bill would cap trustee investment in single issuer at 20 percent
stories.e: The House of Representatives is considering the Trustee Investment Bill 2026, which would replace a 1957 trustee law and cap how much of a trust portfolio covering inheritances, widow funds and charitable assets can sit with a single issuer at 20 percent. Committee chair Solomon Bob said the old law predates a capital market now worth over N80 trillion and newer instruments like REITs and green bonds. The Speaker office said the bill aims to balance protecting trust assets with generating returns for long-term national development.

stories.h: Report: Nigeria has lost N4.6 trillion to building collapses since 2022
stories.e: A forensic-investigators' assessment estimates that building collapses across Nigeria between 2022 and 2025 destroyed about N4.6 trillion worth of property and business assets, with Lagos accounting for more than half of recorded incidents. Experts blame substandard materials, weak construction supervision and poor enforcement, and are calling for stronger regulatory oversight of the building sector.

stories.h: Nigerian stock market crosses N165 trillion as NGX index hits record high
stories.e: The total value of shares on the Nigerian Exchange climbed past N165 trillion for the first time, with the all-share index setting a fresh all-time high. The milestone underscores a strong rally in Nigerian equities even as the wider economy grapples with high borrowing costs and currency pressure.

stories.h: OPay shelves New York listing plans, ends underwriting agreement
stories.e: Nigerian fintech giant OPay has walked back its push for a dual stock market listing, terminating its underwriting agreement and dropping plans to float shares on a New York exchange for now. The reversal raises questions about the hurdles fast-growing African fintechs face when trying to tap international capital markets.

stories.h: MTN Nigeria's cash tax payments jump over 1,200% to N295bn in nine months
stories.e: MTN Nigeria paid N295.4 billion in cash income tax for the nine months to September 2026, roughly 13 times the N21.5 billion paid a year earlier, even as its reported tax expense rose a smaller 67.6% to N630.5 billion. The telecom giant's revenue grew 23.6% to N4.61 trillion and profit after tax rose 55.3%, highlighting how reliant government revenue is on a handful of large corporate taxpayers.

stories.h: Nigeria's debt servicing bill dwarfs combined budgets for five key sectors
stories.e: Nigeria's N15.8 trillion debt-servicing allocation in the 2026 budget exceeds the combined N12.64 trillion set aside for agriculture, health, works, defence and education, according to an October assessment by CFG Advisory. Debt servicing alone consumes 23.1% of the N68.32 trillion federal budget, more than total capital spending, prompting calls for a compliance audit under the Fiscal Responsibility Act as external debt is projected to near $60 billion by year-end.

stories.h: MTN Nigeria's profit jumps 55% on surging data demand
stories.e: MTN Nigeria posted a 55% rise in nine-month profit to N1.17 trillion, driven largely by data revenue as subscribers consumed more data each month, even as a sharp rise in tax expenses ate into the gains. The telecom giant's fintech unit, however, saw revenue fall after regulators suspended its airtime-and-data-credit service for several months earlier in the year.

stories.h: Diaspora remittances hit record $1.57bn in second quarter, NiDCOM says
stories.e: Nigeria's diaspora commission says money sent home through licensed transfer operators reached a record $1.57 billion between April and June, roughly a third higher than the same period last year, crediting central bank reforms for the jump. The figure is part of a wider push to grow formal remittance channels as the naira continues to stabilise.

stories.h: OPay pulls planned $304m New York IPO after foreign regulatory inquiry
stories.e: Nigerian fintech giant OPay withdrew its planned US stock market listing, which would have raised around $304 million at a valuation above $4 billion, after disclosing an unnamed foreign regulatory inquiry. The company said the probe involves a jurisdiction immaterial to its core operations and insisted it would not affect services for its Nigerian customers. The reversal comes only weeks after OPay secured approval for a separate listing on the Nigerian Exchange.

stories.h: OPay pulls $304 million NYSE listing hours after pricing shares
stories.e: SoftBank-backed fintech OPay withdrew its planned $304 million US stock listing shortly after pricing shares at $19 each, just before trading was due to begin on the NYSE. The company said the move followed an inquiry from a regulator in a foreign jurisdiction it described as immaterial to its core business, and that it expects the matter to be resolved soon. The abrupt reversal raises questions about how ready Nigerian fintechs are for the scrutiny of US capital markets.

stories.h: BUA Foods' nine-month profit climbs to N450.5bn despite falling revenue
stories.e: BUA Foods reported an 11% rise in nine-month net profit to N450.5 billion even as turnover fell by about 19% amid weaker demand for its flour and sugar products. The company said sharp cuts in raw-material and administrative costs helped push its EBITDA margin above 43%, up from roughly 31% a year earlier.

stories.h: Nigerian fintech OPay lists on NYSE, raises $304 million in IPO at over $4 billion valuation
stories.e: OPay began trading on the New York Stock Exchange, selling 16 million depositary shares at $19 apiece to raise roughly $304 million and value the Lagos-founded fintech at more than $4 billion. The listing marks one of the largest-ever US market debuts for an African-founded technology company.

stories.h: Dangote Cement nine-month profit jumps 31% as revenue hits N3.8 trillion
stories.e: Dangote Cement posted a 31% rise in nine-month after-tax profit to roughly N975 billion, with revenue climbing to about N3.8 trillion, helped by lower finance costs and reduced foreign exchange losses. The results, covering the period through September 2026, lifted the companys share price on the Nigerian Exchange.

stories.h: CBN-published study links Nigeria's budget deficits directly to naira depreciation
stories.e: A study published in the Central Bank of Nigeria's own Journal of Applied Statistics found that government budget deficits are a major driver of the naira's decline, with fiscal imbalances feeding on themselves over time through tighter money supply and delayed interest-rate pressure. The research, covering data from 1981 to 2024, recommends a binding legal cap on the deficit relative to GDP and a non-oil fiscal stabilisation fund to curb the pattern.

stories.h: 88% of African banks and fintechs report rising digital fraud, Deloitte survey finds
stories.e: Deloitte's latest African Financial Industry Barometer, presented at the Africa Financial Summit in Luanda, found that 88% of surveyed banks and fintech firms across the continent, including Nigerian institutions, reported an increase in digital fraud attempts, well above the overall industry average of 66%. The findings point to mounting cybersecurity pressure on African financial institutions as more customers shift to digital banking channels.

stories.h: Bank of Industry, IFC Sign $50 Million Deal to Expand MSME Financing
stories.e: The Bank of Industry has signed a $50 million loan agreement with the International Finance Corporation aimed at expanding access to finance for Nigerian micro, small and medium enterprises. The deal is intended to help MSMEs, which make up a large share of Nigerian employment, access more affordable credit.

stories.h: CBN eases cash mop-up as N13.79trn in liquidity set to hit banks in November
stories.e: The Central Bank of Nigeria has scaled back its open market operations after aggressively draining banking-system cash in prior months, with analysts projecting about N13.79 trillion in fresh liquidity inflows this November, slightly above October's total. Most of the inflow is expected from maturing OMO bills, with smaller shares from FAAC disbursements and treasury bill maturities. Market watchers caution that how much of this actually reaches lendable bank funds will depend on government cash movements and new debt issuances.

stories.h: Access Holdings' Nine-Month Profit Rises 6% to N474.2 Billion
stories.e: Access Holdings reported a 6 percent year-on-year increase in net profit to N474.2 billion for the first nine months of 2026. The results add to a mixed picture among Nigeria's major banks as they navigate high interest rates and currency pressures this year.

stories.h: FMDA projects N13.79trn in market liquidity for November as CBN eases OMO mop-up
stories.e: Dealers' association FMDA expects Nigeria's financial system to receive N13.79 trillion in inflows this month, driven mostly by maturing OMO bills and FAAC allocations. The forecast follows the Central Bank slowing its liquidity withdrawals in October, when it issued far fewer new OMO securities than the amount maturing, nearly tripling banking-system liquidity from September's level.

stories.h: CBN injects N3.20trn into banking system as maturing debt outpaces new auctions
stories.e: The Central Bank of Nigeria added a net N3.20 trillion in liquidity to the banking system recently, after repayments on maturing government securities exceeded the amount raised through fresh auctions. The resulting cash surplus can push down short-term interbank borrowing rates and ripple through wider lending costs. Market watchers are now waiting to see whether the CBN moves to mop up some of the excess liquidity to keep its tightening stance intact.

stories.h: VFD Group's nine-month profit nearly doubles to N13 billion
stories.e: Investment firm VFD Group reported a 96% jump in net profit for the first nine months of 2026, rising to N13 billion, driven largely by a surge in investment income. Total assets also grew by nearly 30% over the period, reflecting a strong year for the firm's investment portfolio.

stories.h: Binance hack renews scrutiny of customer fund safety in Nigeria's $59bn crypto market
stories.e: A multibillion-dollar theft linked to a breach at crypto exchange Binance, reportedly tied to North Korean hackers, is reviving concerns over how safe Nigerian customer funds are on international trading platforms. Nigeria's crypto market is estimated at $59 billion, and the incident has triggered a wave of customer withdrawals and fresh calls for stronger safeguards.

stories.h: Nigeria's biggest banks post Africa's lowest loan-to-deposit ratios
stories.e: Nigeria's largest banking groups recorded the five lowest loan-to-deposit ratios among major African lenders in 2025, a sign that ongoing bank recapitalisation is squeezing how much credit flows to businesses and households. The finding points to a widening gap between banks' swelling capital bases and their actual lending to the real economy.

stories.h: CBN overhauls agents monitoring Nigeria's crude oil export terminals
stories.e: The Central Bank of Nigeria has appointed eight pre-shipment inspection agents and two monitoring firms to oversee export terminals including Bonga, Forcados and Agbami, reassigning which companies track shipments under the Nigerian Export Supervision Scheme. The changes, set out in an October 29 circular, direct banks, Customs, NNPC and oil operators to comply with the revised oversight arrangement that took effect October 2.

stories.h: Naira gives back 42% of its Q3 gains, closes October at N1,346/$
stories.e: After three straight months of appreciation, the naira weakened through October to close the month at N1,346 to the dollar, down from N1,329.50 at the end of September. Nairametrics reports the currency swung as low as N1,370/$ during the month despite Nigeria's foreign reserves hitting a record $46 billion, with no single factor clearly explaining the reversal.

stories.h: Bankers' institute presses lenders to channel recapitalisation funds to small businesses
stories.e: At its annual fellowship investiture in Lagos, the Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria urged banks to stop concentrating credit on large corporations and instead direct freshly raised capital toward small and medium enterprises, which it says make up nearly half of GDP. A policy economist at the event noted that manufacturing-sector lending has actually shrunk even as banks grew their balance sheets through recapitalisation.

stories.h: OPay pulls $304m NYSE listing days after pricing shares, cites foreign regulatory probe
stories.e: Nigerian-founded fintech OPay abruptly terminated its planned New York Stock Exchange listing just two days after signing its underwriting agreement, citing an unspecified regulatory inquiry in a foreign jurisdiction it called immaterial to its core business. The $304 million offering had valued the SoftBank-backed company at more than $4 billion, and OPay says normal operations in Nigeria and other markets will continue while it works to resolve the issue.

stories.h: DMO rejects N1.84 trillion in bids at latest Treasury bills auction
stories.e: Nigeria's Debt Management Office allotted just N71.16 billion out of nearly N1.9 trillion in bids at its October 28 Treasury bills auction, rejecting the vast majority of investor demand for the second straight sale. The one-year stop rate edged down to 15.80%, even as banking-system liquidity rose sharply on the maturity of prior central bank operations.

stories.h: UBA Becomes First Nigerian Bank to Enable Google Pay for Visa, Mastercard Customers
stories.e: United Bank for Africa says it is the first bank in Nigeria to switch on Google Pay for eligible Visa and Mastercard holders, letting customers tap their phones to pay instead of carrying a physical card. The rollout follows Google Wallet's broader launch in Nigeria and relies on tokenisation infrastructure built with card networks and payment processors. It is part of a wider push by Nigerian banks to modernise digital payments as contactless transactions gain traction.

stories.h: DMO rejects N1.84 trillion bids, pushes T-bill rates lower
stories.e: The Debt Management Office rejected N1.84 trillion worth of bids at its latest Treasury bills auction, a move that pushed yields lower as the government manages domestic borrowing costs. The rejection reflects the DMO's strategy of resisting investor demands for higher returns even amid strong demand for short-term government debt.

stories.h: Fidelity Bank Plc redeems $400 million Eurobond at maturity
stories.e: Fidelity Bank has fully repaid a $400 million Eurobond on its maturity date, a transaction seen as a signal of the lender's financial strength and continued access to international capital markets. The repayment comes as Nigerian banks navigate a tighter global funding environment.

stories.h: Only 59% of Nigerian banks and fintechs ready for CBN's January 2027 data localisation deadline
stories.e: A NITDA survey conducted October 13-27 found that just 26 of 44 responding financial institutions had completed or were likely to complete the steps needed to comply with the CBN's new rule requiring payment data generated in Nigeria to be stored on local servers. Fifteen institutions said compliance by the January 1, 2027 deadline was unlikely, and 22 had not yet begun implementation work such as budgeting and system migration.

stories.h: Nigeria posts Africa's sharpest inflation drop as naira stability aids disinflation
stories.e: Nigeria's headline inflation eased to 14.63% in September from 15.39% in August, its fourth straight monthly decline and the lowest rate since January 2025, giving it the steepest annual drop among Africa's ten largest economies. Analysts linked the slowdown to a more stable naira, among the best-performing African currencies this year, which has eased imported-inflation pressure and supported the central bank's recent 350-basis-point rate cut. Food inflation, however, stayed stubbornly high near 19.6%, showing price relief has not reached everyday staples.

stories.h: Indorama commits $261m to a fourth fertiliser production line in Nigeria
stories.e: Indorama has issued a letter of award to South Korea's Daewoo for a new $261 million ammonia-urea line at its Eleme complex near Port Harcourt, a project that would lift the company's installed Nigerian urea capacity by about a third. The expansion comes as Gulf shipping disruptions have pushed global urea prices to multi-year highs.

stories.h: BUA Cement, Nigerian Breweries among firms quitting the national grid for private power
stories.e: Regulatory filings show BUA Cement, Nigerian Breweries and several other manufacturers and public institutions secured permits for nearly 55 megawatts of captive power generation in the first half of 2026, as repeated grid collapses push major electricity users to go it alone. The Manufacturers Association of Nigeria says its members' spending on alternative power rose more than 20% to over ₦1.3 trillion in 2025, and analysts warn the exodus of big customers could further strain the national grid's finances.

stories.h: Dangote Launches $2.5bn Fuel Storage and Pipeline Project in Namibia
stories.e: Aliko Dangote has broken ground on a $2.5 billion fuel storage and pipeline project near Namibia's Walvis Bay port, targeting landlocked southern African markets that rely on imported petroleum. The facility will include roughly four million barrels of storage capacity and is tied to a proposed 1,700-kilometre pipeline linking Namibia to Botswana and South Africa.

stories.h: Nigeria's biggest firms hit by fourfold surge in energy costs
stories.e: Nigeria's largest listed companies spent nearly four times more on energy in the first half of 2026 compared with a year earlier, driven by rising fuel prices. The surge adds pressure to manufacturers' already tight margins and raises fresh concerns about the cost of doing business in Nigeria's industrial sector.

stories.h: BUA Foods posts 11% profit growth despite falling revenue
stories.e: BUA Foods reported an 11% rise in nine-month profit to N450.47 billion even as revenue fell 19% to N1.15 trillion amid weaker consumer demand and lower prices. The company credited cost management and productivity gains for widening its profit margin despite softer sales.

stories.h: Dangote weighs up to $15bn refining and petrochemicals investment in Egypt
stories.e: Aliko Dangote is in talks with Egyptian officials over a potential $10-15 billion investment focused on oil refining and petrochemicals, aimed at turning Egypt from a fuel importer into a net exporter. The discussions followed a visit to Dangote's Lagos headquarters by Egypt's investment minister, and the final scale of the deal is still being negotiated.

stories.h: Beta Glass's nine-month profit falls 8% as finance costs and FX losses bite
stories.e: Packaging manufacturer Beta Glass saw after-tax profit slip 8.4% to N24.93 billion for the nine months to September, even though revenue rose nearly 5%, as finance costs jumped 45% and the company swung to a foreign-exchange loss. Nairametrics notes the company's third-quarter profit actually grew on its own, showing the annual decline was driven mainly by earlier-year pressures.

stories.h: Manufacturing credit falls 34% despite N4.65trn bank recapitalisation, economists warn
stories.e: New figures presented at a Lagos banking event show credit to Nigerian manufacturers has dropped by about a third since December 2024, even as lenders raised N4.65 trillion in fresh capital, with banks instead favouring oil and gas, trade and government securities. Economic analysts are calling for a coordinated financing framework, warning that industrial growth is being starved of credit despite stronger bank balance sheets.

stories.h: Nigeria's top cement makers post combined N1.71trn profit in nine months
stories.e: Nigeria's three major cement producers posted a combined 37.8% rise in nine-month profit to N1.71 trillion, driven largely by stronger margins and cost efficiencies rather than higher sales volumes. The results underline the sector's continued profitability even as high construction costs remain a strain on ordinary Nigerians.

stories.h: Manufacturers face fresh squeeze on rising diesel prices
stories.e: Nigerian manufacturers are facing renewed cost pressure as diesel prices climb again, squeezing already thin margins for firms that rely on generators amid unreliable grid electricity. Industry groups warn the latest increase could further erode the sector's competitiveness and slow production.

stories.h: Manufacturers spent ₦1.35trn on alternative power in 2025 as sector shed nearly 19,000 jobs
stories.e: Manufacturers Association of Nigeria data presented at an industry AGM shows local manufacturers spent an estimated ₦1.35 trillion on alternative power in 2025, a 23% jump from the prior year, while the sector lost 18,935 jobs in the first half of 2025 alone, nearly double the losses recorded a year earlier. The figures point to unreliable grid supply, with delivered power still far below estimated industrial demand despite rising installed capacity.

stories.h: MAN: manufacturers still borrowing at 30% despite bank recapitalisation
stories.e: The Manufacturers Association of Nigeria says its members are still borrowing at around 30% interest even after banks completed a recapitalisation exercise meant to expand lending, with association president Ifeanyi Okoye contrasting this with Chinese manufacturers who can access credit as cheap as 3%. Speaking at the Nigerian Economic Summit, he said only token rate cuts have reached manufacturers, leaving them at a cost disadvantage against foreign competitors.

stories.h: Nigeria to begin mass production of military munitions within a year, says defence minister
stories.e: Defence Minister Christopher Musa told delegates at Nigeria first Africa International Defence Exhibition in Lagos that local production of defence hardware for domestic use and export to other African countries will start within a year. The head of the Defence Industries Corporation of Nigeria pledged to expand production capacity, with the event drawing officials from more than 20 African countries.

stories.h: Manufacturers cut forex demand by $1bn through local sourcing
stories.e: Nigerian manufacturers reduced their foreign exchange needs by roughly $1 billion in the first half of 2026 as more firms source raw materials locally instead of importing them, according to new industry data. The shift toward backward integration reflects a wider push by producers to cut costs amid ongoing currency pressures.

stories.h: Manufacturers Association to Launch Industrial Energy Cost Reduction Programme in November
stories.e: The Manufacturers Association of Nigeria said it will roll out a new programme next month aimed at helping member companies cut their energy costs, which have become one of the biggest drags on local production. The initiative responds to years of complaints from manufacturers about high electricity tariffs and unreliable power supply squeezing already-thin margins. Details on specific cost-saving measures are expected to be unveiled closer to the launch date.

stories.h: $5bn Ajaokuta steel revival still stalled by power and supply problems
stories.e: A fresh push to revive the long-dormant, $5 billion Ajaokuta Steel Complex is running into the same obstacles that have stalled the plant for decades, including unreliable power supply and shortages of raw materials, according to BusinessDay. The report underscores how one of Nigeria's biggest unfinished public infrastructure investments remains far from generating the industrial jobs and output officials have long promised.

stories.h: Dangote plans additional $1.5bn expansion of Kenya Pipeline network
stories.e: Aliko Dangote plans to invest an additional $1.5 billion to expand Kenya Pipeline Company's network, days after buying a 25% stake in the state-linked firm through a roughly $327 million share purchase on the Nairobi Securities Exchange. The move builds on Dangote's wider push into East African energy infrastructure, which also includes a planned $16 billion refinery in Lamu.

stories.h: Business chamber says Nigeria needs more manufacturing investment to reach $1trn economy
stories.e: A deputy president of the Abuja Chamber of Commerce and Industry told a business lecture in Abuja that Nigeria must channel far more capital into manufacturing and fix unreliable electricity supply to convert recent macroeconomic gains into real industrial growth. He noted manufacturing attracted only a small fraction of foreign direct investment in early 2026, despite government ambitions for a trillion-dollar economy.

stories.h: Chemical Engineers Seek Private Control of Moribund Refineries
stories.e: The Nigerian Society of Chemical Engineers has called on the Federal Government to privatise the country's state-owned refineries in Port Harcourt, Warri and Kaduna through a transparent, time-bound competitive process, rather than continuing to fund repeated failed rehabilitation efforts. The group's president proposed a 22-month transition plan covering asset assessment, investor bidding and ownership transfer, with government retaining only a minority stake. The proposal responds to more than two decades of costly, unsuccessful attempts to revive the plants.

stories.h: Manufacturing Activity Falls 10 Percent as Cement Sector Slides Into Contraction
stories.e: The Nigerian Economic Summit Group's Business Confidence Monitor shows manufacturing activity dropped roughly 10 percent in September, driven largely by a contraction in cement production alongside declines in chemicals, plastics, steel and auto assembly. NESG attributes the slowdown to persistent energy shortages, raw-material shortages, high rents and tight credit, which it says are raising production costs and discouraging new industrial investment.

stories.h: Bandits terrorise eight Taraba communities, residents say 10 of 15 captives freed
stories.e: Residents of eight communities in Karim-Lamido, Taraba State, say armed men have been raiding farms, looting shops and sexually assaulting women for weeks, warning villagers against reporting attacks to security agencies. A community leader said 10 of 15 people abducted in recent raids have been released, while two more farmers were attacked near the Taraba-Plateau border days later; police said they had no record of the incidents at the time of reporting, highlighting a gap between community accounts and official response in Nigeria's rural security crisis.

stories.h: Bandits kill soldier and pregnant woman, abduct over 15 residents in Taraba
stories.e: Suspected bandits attacked the Kuka Sarkin Yamma and Ruwan-Zafi communities in Taraba State's Karim-Lamido area, killing a soldier, a local hunter and a pregnant woman, and abducting more than 15 residents during the raid. The attack came roughly two weeks after a similar assault on nearby Binnari village killed dozens, and as of publication, police had made no official statement on the latest incident.

stories.h: Amnesty International Demands Release of Man Held Over Critical Posts About APC Rally
stories.e: Amnesty International Nigeria is calling for the immediate release of a man it says was detained solely for posting criticism online about a ruling party rally. The rights group argues the detention violates his freedom of expression and sets a troubling precedent for how authorities treat government critics.

stories.h: Investigation: University of Jos hostels, classrooms remain inaccessible for students with disabilities
stories.e: A Premium Times investigation found wheelchair users and visually impaired students at the University of Jos navigate hostels without ramps or grab rails, overgrown and uneven compound paths, and classrooms lacking accessibility features. Students described relying on non-disabled classmates just to reach lectures, while one visually impaired student was injured in a fall on campus last year. University management did not respond to the findings, and the national disability rights commission also did not comment.

stories.h: Investigation: how Nigerian security agencies use surveillance to track and silence critics
stories.e: A new ICIR investigation pulls together a dozen cases of Nigerians, including activists, journalists, and ordinary citizens, allegedly tracked through phone interception, call records, and other monitoring tools, often leading to arrest or detention. Named cases include a protest organiser traced through an associate's phone and a radio presenter who says his calls were tapped for weeks before his arrest. The report says oversight of these tools remains weak, even as public money continues to go toward expanding surveillance infrastructure.

stories.h: PDP Petitions Police Chief Over Alleged Harassment, Killing of Members in Ebonyi
stories.e: The Peoples Democratic Party has formally petitioned the Inspector-General of Police, alleging that its members in Ebonyi State have been subjected to harassment and, in some cases, killed. The party is demanding an investigation into the claims as political tensions rise ahead of the 2027 election cycle.

stories.h: Gunmen Abduct 14 Students and a Teacher in Niger State Community
stories.e: Suspected terrorists stormed a community in Niger State and abducted 14 students along with one of their teachers, in the latest of a string of mass-kidnapping incidents targeting schools in the region. Security agencies have reportedly been deployed to the area as calls grow for stronger protection of schools in Nigeria's north-central and north-west states.

stories.h: Four Nigerian girls, including a 14-year-old, rescued from traffickers in Mali
stories.e: A joint operation by an anti-trafficking NGO and NAPTIP's Uyo command rescued four girls from Kogi State who had been lured to Mali with promises of mining and shop jobs, then allegedly forced into prostitution. One of the victims, a minor, helped trigger the rescue by sending a distress message after her trafficker confiscated the group's phones and identification. The girls are now receiving medical and psychological support as authorities are urged to pursue the trafficking network behind their ordeal.

stories.h: Gunmen abduct 14 Islamic school students from farm in Niger State
stories.e: Suspected bandits seized at least 14 students of an Islamic school while they were helping their teacher harvest maize in Tungan-Bako village, Rafi local government area of Niger State, police said. Security operatives have launched a rescue operation, though no update on the students' whereabouts had been given as of publication.

stories.h: SSS frees four men held nearly four years over false IPOB links, pays N20m compensation
stories.e: The State Security Service released four men from Bayelsa State who had been detained since May 2022 on suspicion of IPOB membership, after a review found they had been misled by scammers promising a federal amnesty stipend rather than genuinely involved with the group. Each man will receive N5 million in compensation plus medical and psychological support, part of a wider case review the SSS head launched after taking office.

stories.h: Ebonyi governor proposes death penalty for kidnapping after traditional ruler murder
stories.e: Ebonyi Governor Francis Nwifuru sent a bill to the state assembly that would make kidnapping a capital offence with no lesser punishment, announcing the move at the funeral of traditional ruler Francis Igwe, who was abducted on his way to church and later found dead. Nwifuru said the law is meant to deter kidnappings carried out for political or financial motives. The proposal adds to a broader national debate over whether harsher sentencing can curb the kidnapping crisis facing Nigeria.

stories.h: Women engineers, advocates push Nigeria to end child marriage
stories.e: At an Abuja event marking the International Day of the Girl Child, women's and engineering groups called on government and parents to end child marriage and keep girls in school, warning of health risks from early childbirth. They urged stronger enforcement of existing education laws and scholarships for girls from poor households.

stories.h: Gunmen abduct grieving husband and five others escorting wife's corpse in Benue
stories.e: Armed men kidnapped a widower and five others as they transported his late wife's body from Kano to Benue State for burial, abandoning her corpse on the roadside. The kidnappers are reportedly demanding N15 million ransom, and security agencies say they are working to rescue the victims.

stories.h: Katsina government denies campaign rally caused Faskari violence that injured several
stories.e: Katsina State's government says clashes that burnt vehicles and injured people in Yankara, Faskari, stemmed from a dispute over a religious procession route rather than Governor Dikko Radda's nearby campaign rally, as some accounts had claimed. A political association chairman said his convoy, travelling to the rally, was caught up in the violence and lost a vehicle, though its occupants escaped unharmed.

stories.h: Police say they repelled terrorist attack in Zamfara, found over 30 bandit bodies
stories.e: Police in Zamfara State report repelling an attack by armed terrorists, after which more than 30 bodies believed to belong to the attackers were discovered, in the latest clash in a state that has endured years of banditry. Full details of the operation and independent verification of the casualty figures are still emerging.

stories.h: Security agencies rescue three Zamfara clerics kidnapped en route to prayer session for Tinubu
stories.e: Nigeria's national security office and the DSS freed three clergymen who were abducted in Zamfara State while travelling to a prayer session organised in support of President Tinubu. Reports indicate operations are continuing to secure the release of other captives still being held from the same incident. The abduction underscores the persistent insecurity facing religious leaders and ordinary civilians in parts of northern Nigeria.

stories.h: Panel finds NSCDC officers negligent in deaths of 33 detainees, including 14 children, in Niger State
stories.e: A federal investigative panel examining the deaths of 33 people, including 14 children, held in a civil defence detention cell in Minna found officers authorised an unapproved raid, crammed dozens of detainees into one cell, and ignored warnings and cries for help over several hours. The panel recommended that the suspended commandant and several colleagues be dismissed and criminally prosecuted for offences including murder and torture, with the case now referred to the Attorney-General.

stories.h: El-Rufai marks 256th day in detention, appeals to Trump and Macron for a fair trial
stories.e: Former Kaduna governor Nasir El-Rufai marked his 256th day in detention by publicly appealing to international leaders and rights bodies, including the UN and Amnesty International, saying a fair trial is not an act of mercy. He has been held since February 2026 after honouring an EFCC invitation, and his family has long disputed the legality of the ICPC detention order.

stories.h: Gunmen kill four in Plateau community despite state-imposed curfew
stories.e: Suspected gunmen attacked Sabon Angwa community in Barkin Ladi council area of Plateau State around 8pm, killing at least four people even though a dusk-to-dawn curfew was in force. A resident said authorities had been warned of a possible attack a day earlier, and a local youth group is demanding faster security response to early warnings.

stories.h: Detainees drank urine and sweat before 33 died in NSCDC Niger cell, probe finds
stories.e: An independent investigation into the deaths of 33 detainees held by the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps in Niger State found that officers packed around 50 people, including children, into a tiny, poorly ventilated cell with no running water, ignoring warnings that overcrowding could cause suffocation. The panel rejected the agency's earlier claim that a disease outbreak was to blame and recommended prosecuting the officers involved.

stories.h: Nigerian-born scholar Dapo Akande elected judge of the International Court of Justice
stories.e: Dapo Akande, a Nigerian-born Oxford professor of international law running as the United Kingdom's candidate, has been elected to a nine-year term on the International Court of Justice, the UN's top judicial body. He will take his seat on the Hague-based court in February 2027. His election highlights the continued influence of Nigerian-trained legal scholars within major international institutions.

stories.h: Mo Ibrahim warns Africa is backsliding into a 'strongman' era
stories.e: Sudanese-British billionaire Mo Ibrahim says the continent's governance gains have stalled and that authoritarian 'strongmen' are resurging, tying the trend to a broader global drift away from democratic norms. He pointed to his foundation's governance index, which he says shows little improvement across much of Africa in recent years, as a warning sign for citizens and policymakers alike.

stories.h: Nigeria, Russia agree to renegotiate 59-year-old aviation pact
stories.e: Nigeria's aviation minister Festus Keyamo met Russian officials at the Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow and agreed to renegotiate the countries' 1967 bilateral air services agreement, with both sides aiming to finalise a new deal in Saint Petersburg by April 2027. Neither side has yet disclosed what routes or airlines the updated agreement would cover.

stories.h: Nigeria, Russia agree to replace 59-year-old aviation agreement
stories.e: Nigeria's aviation minister Festus Keyamo and Russian officials agreed, on the sidelines of the Third Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow, to renegotiate the countries' 1967 air services pact. Both sides have set up negotiating teams and aim to sign a replacement agreement in Saint Petersburg in April 2027, though no route or airline details have been disclosed yet.

stories.h: CAR tightens border checks as DR Congo Ebola cases rise
stories.e: The Central African Republic has tightened checks at its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo as an Ebola outbreak there continues to spread into new provinces. The heightened screening aims to prevent cross-border transmission as regional health authorities scale up containment efforts.

stories.h: Russian drone strike kills 14 at Ukraine train station
stories.e: A Russian drone strike on a train station in Ukraine has killed 14 people, in what officials described as a horrific attack on civilian infrastructure. The strike adds to the mounting civilian toll of Russia's continuing war against Ukraine.

stories.h: Nigeria joins 129 other nations at UN in demanding end to US embargo on Cuba
stories.e: Nigeria was among 130 countries that backed a UN General Assembly resolution calling for an end to the decades-old US economic embargo on Cuba, a vote the US and Israel opposed and 25 nations abstained from. Most African states supported the resolution, which has passed annually since 1992 and comes as fresh US sanctions have deepened Cuba's economic strain.

stories.h: Nigeria downgrades delegation to Russia-Africa summit, keeps Tinubu and VP away
stories.e: Nigeria sent only Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Sola Enikanolaiye to the two-day Russia-Africa summit in Moscow, after earlier plans for Vice President Kashim Shettima to lead the delegation were quietly dropped without explanation from the presidency. Analysts link the low-key presence to Nigeria's deepening ties with the United States and the approaching 2027 election campaign.

stories.h: DRC Ebola outbreak passes 10,000 cases, nearly 5,000 deaths, as WHO cites hopeful signs
stories.e: The Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak, now the world's second-deadliest on record, has passed 10,000 confirmed cases and nearly 5,000 deaths, health authorities reported. The WHO's Africa director said rising case numbers reflect a heavy toll but pointed to over 2,600 recoveries and advancing vaccine trials as reasons for cautious optimism, while noting infections linked to the outbreak have already surfaced in Kenya and Nigeria.

stories.h: Uganda orders 21-day quarantine for travellers from DR Congo as Ebola spreads
stories.e: Uganda has imposed a mandatory 21-day quarantine on citizens returning from the Democratic Republic of Congo, as health authorities work to contain an Ebola outbreak in the region that has also produced a confirmed case in Nigeria. The measure reflects growing concern across East and West Africa about the virus's spread.

stories.h: Ebola cases in DR Congo surpass 10,000 in fastest-growing outbreak on record
stories.e: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has now infected more than 10,000 people, making it the fastest-growing epidemic of the disease that health authorities have tracked. Neighbouring countries including Uganda and Kenya have tightened border and quarantine measures as the virus keeps crossing into other parts of the region.

stories.h: Attackers kill nurse responding to Ebola case in DR Congo
stories.e: Assailants killed a nurse and wounded another health worker who were responding to an Ebola case in the Democratic Republic of Congo, underscoring the security risks facing medical teams fighting the outbreak. The attack has added to mounting concern among global health officials about containing the virus' spread across multiple African countries.

stories.h: WHO Says Nigeria Has No Active Ebola Cases After Patient's Evacuation to Switzerland
stories.e: The World Health Organization's Africa regional director said Nigeria currently has no active Ebola cases after the infected patient and her husband were medically evacuated out of the country. Nigerian health workers treated the patient through the acute phase of her illness before she was stabilized and flown out, with Switzerland now managing her continued care. WHO urged continued vigilance in monitoring the dozens of contacts still being tracked within Nigeria.

stories.h: Lula wins historic fourth term as Brazil's president, Bolsonaro refuses to concede
stories.e: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva defeated Flavio Bolsonaro in Brazil's presidential runoff, winning about 51.8% of the vote to become the first candidate since Brazil's return to democracy to win after trailing in the first round. Bolsonaro has refused to concede and is seeking to have the results annulled, extending political uncertainty in Latin America's largest democracy.

stories.h: Nurse killed, health worker injured in attack on Ebola responders in DRC
stories.e: The World Health Organisation reported that a nurse was killed and another health worker seriously hurt in an attack on an Ebola response team in Bafwasende, eastern DRC. WHO leaders condemned the assault as part of a pattern of violence against health workers during the ongoing outbreak, which has also produced Nigeria's only imported case, a woman evacuated to Switzerland after traveling from Uganda.

stories.h: Lula wins fourth term as Brazil's president, defeating Bolsonaro's son in runoff
stories.e: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has been re-elected Brazil's president for a fourth term, narrowly beating far-right senator Flavio Bolsonaro, son of the jailed former president, in a runoff held Sunday. Lula took just over 51.7% of the vote, breaking a recent run of right-wing election wins across Latin America, though Bolsonaro has rejected the outcome and says he will seek to have it annulled.

stories.h: Uganda Orders 21-Day Ebola Quarantine for Returnees From DR Congo
stories.e: Uganda has imposed a mandatory 21-day quarantine on citizens returning from the Democratic Republic of Congo as part of efforts to contain a regional Ebola outbreak. The measure comes as neighbouring countries, including Nigeria, step up surveillance and preparedness over fears the virus could spread further across the region.

stories.h: Algeria's Senate Approves Troop Deployment to Niger
stories.e: Algeria's upper house of parliament has approved sending troops to Niger, a move that signals deepening regional security cooperation amid instability in the Sahel. The decision reflects wider concerns about cross-border militant threats affecting West and North Africa.

stories.h: Uganda restricts transit for DRC travellers after Nigeria Ebola case
stories.e: Uganda's health ministry has barred travellers with recent DRC travel history from transiting the country and reinstated locator forms for contact tracing, following an Ebola case detected in Nigeria in a woman who had passed through Uganda. Ugandan officials say she showed no symptoms while in the country and that they are working with Nigerian authorities to trace her movements and possible contacts. Uganda, which declared its own Ebola outbreak over in August, says it remains Ebola-free.

stories.h: Macron cancels state visit to Nigeria; France-Nigeria business forum postponed
stories.e: French President Emmanuel Macron called off a planned state visit to Nigeria, reportedly over concerns that travelling amid ongoing protests at home could look insensitive, alongside Nigerian unease that the trip could draw accusations of foreign interference close to next year's election, and shared worries over a newly confirmed Ebola case in the country. The France-Nigeria Business Forum scheduled for October 29 in Lagos, meant to deepen trade ties between the two countries, has also been postponed with no new date announced. Macron's visit is now expected sometime in 2027 instead.

stories.h: Flamingos reach first-ever U-17 Women's World Cup final after facing Brazil in semis
stories.e: Nigeria's Flamingos took on Brazil in Rabat for a place in Saturday's FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup final, a stage the team has never reached before in the tournament's history. The match drew heavy attention from Nigerian sports fans hoping to see the junior women's team deliver a rare global trophy run. A win would mark a milestone for Nigerian women's football development at the youth level.

stories.h: One player killed, several injured in road accident involving Nigerian girls' football academy
stories.e: A player with the Ayisat Yusuf Football Academy died and several teammates were injured when their team's vehicle was involved in a road accident while travelling from Ogun State to a league fixture in Lagos. The academy's founder confirmed the death but has not released further details on how the crash occurred. The team's driver also sustained serious injuries, with some players reportedly requiring urgent medical care.

stories.h: Tinubu Fulfils $100,000 Cash Promise to Super Falcons After WAFCON Win
stories.e: President Bola Tinubu's promised $100,000 cash reward to each member of the Super Falcons for their WAFCON title victory has now been paid out, months after the pledge was first announced. The payout, alongside earlier national honours and housing pledges, had previously drawn public debate over the scale of rewards for athletes compared with other national priorities.

stories.h: Nigeria's Flamingos reach U-17 Women's World Cup semi-final
stories.e: Nigeria's Flamingos defeated Venezuela 1-0 in a tense quarter-final at the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup in Morocco, with captain Azeezat Oduntan converting a late penalty in the 89th minute. The win sends Nigeria to the semi-finals for only the second time in the tournament's history.

stories.h: Flamingos beat Venezuela to set up U-17 World Cup semi-final against Brazil
stories.e: Nigeria's U-17 women's team, the Flamingos, defeated Venezuela in their quarter-final at the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup in Morocco, setting up a semi-final meeting with Brazil. The win keeps alive Nigeria's bid for a first title at the tournament and has drawn growing public attention back home as the team continues its run.

stories.h: Flamingos eye World Cup semi-final spot as they face Venezuela in quarterfinal
stories.e: Nigeria's U-17 women's team, the Flamingos, take on Venezuela on Sunday in Morocco for a place in the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup semi-finals, following wins over Puerto Rico, defending champions DPR Korea, and Mexico after an opening loss to Poland. Forwards Oluebube Umejiaku and Oluwakemi Adegbuyi have led the attack, while goalkeeper Jane Ijirigho's saves have helped keep the team's run alive.

stories.h: CAF reverses four-year AFCON plan, restores biennial tournament
stories.e: The Confederation of African Football has reversed its plan to move the Africa Cup of Nations to a four-year cycle, restoring the tournaments traditional two-year schedule after months of pushback from national federations and coaches. The U-turn follows a review that CAF president Patrice Motsepe launched earlier in October amid widespread opposition to the 2025 decision.

stories.h: Flamingos Edge Mexico to Reach FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup Quarter-Finals
stories.e: Nigeria's Flamingos defeated Mexico in their Round of 16 clash at the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup in Morocco, with goals from Umejiaku and Dunstan sealing the win. The result sends Nigeria into the quarter-finals, where they are set to face Venezuela on Sunday. It is another strong showing for Nigerian women's youth football on the global stage at this tournament.

stories.h: Osimhen scores twice as Galatasaray beat Fenerbahce to retake Super Lig summit
stories.e: Victor Osimhen scored twice in the first half as Galatasaray beat rivals Fenerbahce 2-1 in the Istanbul derby, sending the Nigerian striker's side back to the top of Turkey's Super Lig. It's the latest strong outing in a season where Osimhen has continued to be one of the league's most prolific forwards.

stories.h: Nigeria shut out as Kane and Putellas crowned world's best at Ballon d'Or
stories.e: Harry Kane and Alexia Putellas won the men's and women's Ballon d'Or at Monday's ceremony in London, the first time the award has been handed out outside Paris. No Nigerian player made this year's shortlist, a sharp drop-off after Victor Osimhen and Ademola Lookman were in contention in recent years.

stories.h: Iheanacho extends scoring streak as Ajayi, Awaziem shine for Nigerians abroad
stories.e: Kelechi Iheanacho scored again for Bursaspor to stretch his streak to 12 consecutive league matches, taking his season tally to 16 goals in 12 games. Semi Ajayi helped Hull City hold Premier League side Brentford to a draw and won man-of-the-match honours, while defender Chidozie Awaziem scored twice in Konyaspor's win in the Turkish league.

stories.h: Nigeria beat Uganda for the first time in 13 attempts to clinch T20 World Cup sub-regional qualifier
stories.e: Nigeria's cricket team finished unbeaten to top a six-nation round-robin in Abuja, beating Uganda along the way for the first time in thirteen previous meetings, and secured one of two tickets out of the sub-regional Africa qualifier. The result sends Nigeria through to the next stage of qualification for the T20 World Cup, with Uganda earning the other qualifying spot.

stories.h: NPFL: Bendel Insurance End Rivers United's Unbeaten Run in Southwest Derby Stalemate
stories.e: Bendel Insurance halted league leaders Rivers United's unbeaten start to the Nigeria Premier Football League season, while a separate Southwest derby ended goalless. The results shake up the title race as the domestic season progresses.

stories.h: Flamingos Face Mexico in FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup Quarter-Final Battle
stories.e: Nigeria's U-17 women's team, the Flamingos, are set to face Mexico as African sides push for a place in the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup quarter-finals. The match represents one of the continent's last chances to advance in the tournament.

stories.h: Nigeria's Flamingos stun defending champions North Korea to reach U-17 Women's World Cup knockouts
stories.e: Nigeria's Flamingos defeated holders Korea DPR 3-1 in Morocco, with goals from Oluwakemi Adegbuyi, Oluebube Umejiaku and Kanyinsola Yusuf securing their place in the Round of 16 at the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup. The win capped a mixed group stage for the young Nigerian side, who had also beaten Puerto Rico but lost to Poland.

stories.h: Nigeria's Flamingos stun defending champions North Korea to reach U-17 Women's World Cup last 16
stories.e: Nigeria's U-17 women's team, the Flamingos, beat two-time defending champions North Korea 3-1 in their final Group B match at the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup in Morocco, securing their place in the Round of 16 after an earlier 2-1 opening loss to Poland and a 2-0 win over Puerto Rico. Head coach Akeem Busari credited the turnaround to the squad refocusing after the Poland setback, noting it was the team's first defeat under him since he took charge in April. The result keeps alive Nigeria's bid to challenge for the title at the tournament co-hosted by Morocco.

stories.h: NFF sticks with Uyo as Super Eagles' home ground for now
stories.e: Nigeria's football federation says it is not yet ready to shift the Super Eagles' home matches to Lagos, keeping Uyo's Godswill Akpabio Stadium as the team's base for the time being. The decision follows a 3-0 home loss to Guinea-Bissau that has left Nigeria trailing in its AFCON 2027 qualifying group. Officials say Lagos' renovated Teslim Balogun Stadium is not yet cleared for international fixtures ahead of next month's qualifiers against Tanzania.

stories.h: Flamingos stun two-time champions North Korea to reach World Cup last 16
stories.e: Nigeria's U-17 women's team beat two-time defending champions Korea DPR 3-1 at the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup in Morocco, with goals from Oluwakemi Adegbuyi, Oluebube Umejiaku and Kanyinsola Yusuf sending them into the knockout round. The win capped a group stage in which Nigeria, Poland and Korea DPR all finished level on six points.

stories.h: FIFA Approves Normalisation Committee to Run Nigerian Football After NFF Mass Resignation
stories.e: FIFA's Council Bureau approved a Normalisation Committee to take over running Nigerian football after the entire NFF leadership, including president Ibrahim Musa Gusau, resigned en masse in August and derailed a planned elective congress. FIFA and CAF will jointly pick the committee's members, who are barred from contesting the eventual NFF election and must hand over power by no later than May 2027. Until then, the federation's secretariat will handle routine administration while the normalisation process unfolds.

stories.h: FIFA approves normalisation committee to run Nigeria Football Federation
stories.e: FIFA has approved a normalisation committee to temporarily run the Nigeria Football Federation after its president, Ibrahim Musa Gusau, and the rest of the executive committee resigned en masse in August, derailing planned elections. The committee, to be jointly appointed by FIFA and CAF, will oversee day-to-day football administration until new elections are held, with its mandate ending no later than May 2027.
